# Tread

> Tread is a small, statically typed programming language built to teach how programming languages work. Its toolchain is written in Go: a lexer, parser, type checker, bytecode compiler, and stack-based virtual machine, each a separate package small enough to read.

Key facts (updated 2026-11-12):

- Motto: "A language for learning how languages work." A tread is one step of a staircase; Tread is learned one stage at a time: lexer, parser, checker, compiler, VM.
- Command: `tread`, with `tread run <file.tr>`, `tread check <file.tr>`, `tread version`, and `tread help`. Source files use the `.tr` extension.
- Error codes: `TR-` plus a phase letter and a number, for example `TR-T001` (type mismatch) or `TR-R003` (call depth exceeded). Runtime errors inside a function print a stack trace.
- Version 0.3.0, experimental. 0.3.0 is not published as a release yet; build from source with Go 1.25 or later.
- Language today: types Int, Float, Bool, String, Unit; `let` and `let mut`; functions with typed parameters and recursion; if / else if / else; string interpolation with `${...}`; `print` and `toString`; checked integer arithmetic.
- Not supported yet: loops (use recursion), collections, user-defined types, generics, imports, and file or network I/O.
- Platforms: macOS 12 or later (Apple silicon, Intel), Linux kernel 3.2 or later (x86-64, ARM64), Windows 10 or Server 2016 or later (x86-64).
- Free and open source under the MIT License. Created by Sarvess Veeriyah.

- [Language tutorial](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/AURA-Advanced_Unified_Runtime_Architecture/blob/main/README.md#language-tutorial): eleven short lessons, each a complete program with its output
- [Language reference](https://github.com/sarvessveeriyah2312/AURA-Advanced_Unified_Runtime_Architecture/blob/main/README.md#language-reference): types, operators, keywords, scope
